```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
source("analysis/synteny/R/functions.R")
cfg <- syn_config()
tab <- function(f) read_tsv(file.path(cfg$tables, f), show_col_types = FALSE)
genomes <- read_genome_table(cfg, all = TRUE)
qc <- tab("genome_qc.tsv")
pi_tab <- tab("pair_indices.tsv") %>% mutate(same_chr = 1 - inter_break)
fits <- tab("decay_fits.tsv")
rates <- tab("rates_by_clade.tsv")
tests <- tab("rate_tests.tsv")
mvals <- tab("matched_values_by_clade.tsv")
mtests <- tab("matched_tests.tsv")
ceiling_tab <- tab("noise_ceiling.tsv")
within <- pi_tab %>% filter(within) %>% mutate(clade = factor(clade, levels = clade_levels))

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))
p_text <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p))
pval <- function(df, idx, cmp, ...) {
  df %>% filter(index == idx, comparison == cmp, ...) %>% pull(median_p) %>% p_text()
}
prim <- function(cmp) pval(tests, "strand_index_norm", cmp, genome_set == "all",
                          divergence == "d_sub", model == "stretched")
mv <- function(idx, cl) mvals %>% filter(index == idx, clade == cl) %>% pull(median_value) %>%
  round(2)
n_indep <- mvals %>% filter(index == "strand_index_norm") %>%
  with(setNames(pairs_per_draw, clade))  # independent pairs per draw, matched window
idx_lab <- c(strand_index_norm = "Strand randomisation index", tau_index_norm = "Kendall's tau index",
             corr_index_norm = "Correlation index", goc_intra_norm = "GOC (vicinity 4)",
             goc1_intra_norm = "Conserved adjacency", same_chr = "Neighbour on same chromosome")
scale_of <- c(strand_index_norm = "meso", tau_index_norm = "meso", corr_index_norm = "meso",
              goc_intra_norm = "micro", goc1_intra_norm = "micro", same_chr = "macro")
pr <- function(a, b) pi_tab %>% filter((.data$a == !!a & .data$b == !!b) | (.data$a == !!b & .data$b == !!a))
fig <- function(f) knitr::include_graphics(file.path(cfg$figures, f), rel_path = FALSE)
n_within <- sum(pi_tab$within)
```

# Summary

**Question.** CENP-A was lost in the ancestor of Umbelopsidales + Mucorales and
CENP-C in the ancestor of Mucorales. Is within-chromosome gene order scrambled
faster, for a given sequence divergence, in these clades than in
Mortierellales, which keep both proteins?

**Answer.**

- **Mucorales: yes.** Gene order and gene orientation within chromosomes decay
  much faster per unit of sequence divergence than in Mortierellales (primary
  test, strand randomisation index: one-sided `r prim("Mucorales > Mortierellales")`;
  Kendall's tau index `r pval(tests, "tau_index_norm", "Mucorales > Mortierellales", genome_set == "all", divergence == "d_sub", model == "stretched")`).
  Among closely related pairs (`r cfg$d_min_rate` < d ≤ 0.15 CDS subs/site),
  the median strand index is `r mv("strand_index_norm", "Mucorales")` in
  Mucorales versus `r mv("strand_index_norm", "Mortierellales")` in
  Mortierellales (model-free test `r pval(mtests, "strand_index_norm", "Mucorales > Mortierellales")`).
- **The excess is within chromosomes.** The rate at which neighbouring genes
  move to *different* chromosomes does not differ between Mucorales and
  Mortierellales (`r pval(tests, "same_chr", "Mucorales > Mortierellales", genome_set == "all", divergence == "d_sub", model == "stretched")`).
  Gene content of chromosomes is kept while order and orientation are lost:
  the mesosynteny pattern of Hane et al. (2011).
- **Umbelopsidales: no.** Umbelopsidales (CENP-A lost, CENP-C kept) scramble no
  faster than Mortierellales on any index (strand index `r prim("Umbelopsidales > Mortierellales")`)
  and slower than Mucorales (`r prim("Mucorales > Umbelopsidales")`).
- **Interpretation.** Accelerated scrambling coincides with the loss of CENP-C
  (and the mosaic centromeres described in *Mucor*), not with the loss of
  CENP-A alone. This is one evolutionary contrast: other Mucorales-specific
  traits could explain it as well (Section [Caveats](#caveats)).
- The preliminary figure's comparison (*M. fragilis* vs *M. plumbeus* at
  d = 0.050 vs *M. zonata* vs *L. hyalina* at 0.056) used an older tree. In the
  current CDS tree the *Mucor* pair is 0.318 subs/site apart. The conclusion
  still holds with properly matched pairs: *M. circinelloides* strains
  (d = `r sprintf("%.3f", pr("gzMucCirc1", "gzMucCirc2")$d_sub)`) and *M. fragilis*
  strains (d = `r sprintf("%.3f", pr("gzMucFrag1", "gzMucFrag2")$d_sub)`) are already
  scrambled, unlike *M. zonata* vs *L. hyalina* (d = `r sprintf("%.3f", pr("ggMorZona1", "gzLinHyal1")$d_sub)`).

Logs: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) (all analysis decisions, including those
made after looking at data) and [LITERATURE.md](LITERATURE.md) (searches and
sources).

# Background

*Mucor circinelloides* lacks CENP-A and CENP-C and has "mosaic" centromeres:
a short kinetochore-binding core flanked by Grem-LINE1 retroelements
(Navarro-Mendoza et al. 2019). Both proteins are absent across Mucorales;
CENP-A is also absent in Umbelopsidales (this project). Losing these proteins
should change centromere organisation, and centromeres constrain which
rearrangements are viable (pericentric inversions, translocations between
centromeres; Coelho et al. 2024, Guin et al. 2020).

*Mesosynteny* (Hane et al. 2011) is conservation of gene content within
homologous chromosomes with randomised gene order and orientation. It was
described in filamentous Ascomycetes, especially Dothideomycetes, and
attributed to frequent intrachromosomal inversions with rare translocations.
Similar patterns, conserved chromosome content with scrambled order, are
known from holocentric lineages that lost CenH3/CENP-A: Lepidoptera
(d'Alençon et al. 2010) and rhabditid nematodes (Coghlan & Wolfe 2002;
Gonzalez de la Rosa et al. 2021). They also occur in monocentric lineages
(*Drosophila* Muller elements, Bhutkar et al. 2008; *Oikopleura*, Plessy et
al. 2024), so the pattern alone is not diagnostic of centromere change. No
published study was found that relates kinetochore gene loss in fungi to the
rate of within-chromosome scrambling.

# Data

```{r data-counts}
n_g <- genomes %>% filter(include == "yes") %>% count(order)
```

- **Genomes:** `r sum(genomes$include == "yes")` Mucoromycota genomes with gene
  coordinates (`r paste(n_g$n, n_g$order, collapse = ", ")`). *Mucor lusitanicus*
  (MucCirc3) is excluded because its OrthoFinder protein IDs cannot be
  linked to its coordinate table (DECISIONS.md D3).
- **Orthologues:** OrthoFinder 2.5.4 pairwise orthologues
  (`data/orthofinder/results/Orthologues`); one-to-one orthologues are used as
  anchors. No Mucoromycota GENESPACE run exists in `Mucor/data` on NeLS (D1).
- **Divergence:** patristic distance on the CDS maximum-likelihood tree
  (substitutions/site; primary); protein distance (OrthoFinder species tree)
  and time (dated tree) as sensitivity analyses.
- **Pairs:** all `r n_within` within-order pairs (plus EBP-Nor pairs across
  orders, not used in the tests). Median `r format(median(pi_tab$n_anchors), big.mark = ",")`
  one-to-one anchors per pair (range `r format(min(pi_tab$n_anchors), big.mark = ",")`–`r format(max(pi_tab$n_anchors), big.mark = ",")`).

```{r qc-table}
qc %>%
  transmute(Genome = genome, Species = species, Order = order, Source = source,
            Genes = genes, `Sequences with genes` = seqs, `Gene N50` = gene_n50,
            `Genes on seqs >=100 genes` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * frac_genes_seq100),
            `OrthoFinder IDs mapped` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * frac_mapped)) %>%
  arrange(Order, Genome) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Genome QC. Gene N50: number of genes on the sequence at which half of all genes are reached in sequences sorted by gene count.")
```

# Methods

**Anchors.** For each genome pair, one-to-one orthologues from the
OrthoFinder pairwise tables are placed on the assemblies. Gene order is the
rank of an anchor among anchors on the same sequence. Relative orientation is
+1 if both genes are on the same strand.

**Indices** (re-implementations for orthologue anchors of published indices;
checked on synthetic genomes in `R/test_functions.R`). Each index is computed
with each genome as reference and the two values are averaged.

| Scale | Index | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| macro | Neighbour on same chromosome | fraction of adjacent anchors whose orthologues are on the same chromosome in the other genome | breakpoint logic of Plessy et al. 2024 |
| macro | Synteny index; macrosynteny fraction | anchors on the best-matching chromosome; anchors on Fisher-significant chromosome pairs | GenomicBreaks; odp, macrosyntR |
| meso | **Strand randomisation index** (primary) | per chromosome and its best-matching partner, `|n_same - n_opposite| / n`, anchor-weighted mean | GenomicBreaks, Plessy et al. 2024 |
| meso | Kendall's tau index; correlation index | `|tau|` of anchor ranks; `|r|` of positions, on the same chromosome pairs | GenomicBreaks (correlation index) |
| micro | GOC; conserved adjacency | adjacent anchors whose orthologues are within 4 (GOC) or 1 anchor(s) on the other chromosome | Rocha 2003; GenomicBreaks |

Within-chromosome indices are normalised to `(observed - random) / (1 - random)`
using 20 shuffles of anchor positions within each chromosome (chromosome
content kept, orientation randomised): 1 = conserved, 0 = as random as
chromosome content allows. The "same chromosome" index is not normalised.

**Decay with divergence.** Each index is modelled as
`I(d) = c * exp(-(lambda * d)^beta)`. The ceiling `c` comes from
`r ceiling_tab$n_pairs[1]` near-identical pairs (d ≤ `r cfg$d_min_rate`);
`beta` (shape) is shared by all clades and estimated per index; `lambda`
is the clade-specific rate. Each pair with `r cfg$d_min_rate` < d ≤ `r cfg$d_max` gets a rate
`lambda_ij = (-log(I_ij / c))^(1/beta) / d_ij`. The range ends just above
the deepest split within Mortierellales and Umbelopsidales, so all clades are
compared over the same range. The model and its shared shape were set after
an interim look at the data (DECISIONS.md D11-D12). The plain exponential
model (`beta = 1`) that was specified first is reported as a sensitivity
analysis.

**Tests.** Pairs share branches, so tests use sets of phylogenetically
independent pairs (paths in the ML tree share no branch; Maddison 2000),
chosen greedily with the shortest paths first and random tie-breaks. Each of
`r cfg$n_draws` draws contains up to 6 Mortierellales, 3 Umbelopsidales and
12 Mucorales pairs. In each draw, one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests compare
per-pair rates between clades. Reported values are the median p over draws
and the fraction of draws with p < 0.05. A model-free test compares raw
index values of independent pairs with `r cfg$d_min_rate` < d ≤ 0.15.

**Pre-specified primary test:** strand randomisation index, CDS distance,
all genomes, Mucorales > Mortierellales and Umbelopsidales > Mortierellales.
The primary index was chosen after a six-pair pilot, before any clade
comparison (D7).

# Results

## Dot plots at matched divergence

```{r fig-main, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = paste0("**Figure 1.** (A) Oxford dot plots of one-to-one orthologues for pairs at similar divergence within each order: top row closely related, bottom row d ≈ 0.45. Points are coloured by gene orientation relative to the other genome, after orienting each chromosome on its main diagonal. Grid lines are sequence boundaries (sequences with ≥ 1.5% of anchors; numbered by size). (B) Indices against CDS divergence for all within-order pairs with d ≤ 0.65, with descriptive LOESS smoothers. Right panel: index values at matched divergence (", cfg$d_min_rate, " < d ≤ 0.15); points are all pairs in this range. Pairs whose paths in the tree share a branch are not independent (a rearrangement on that branch counts in each of them), so bars and p use only sets of phylogenetically independent pairs, whose paths share no branch (Maddison 2000). ", format(cfg$n_draws, big.mark = ","), " such sets were drawn, each with ", n_indep[["Mortierellales"]], " Mortierellales, ", n_indep[["Umbelopsidales"]], " Umbelopsidales and ", n_indep[["Mucorales"]], " Mucorales pairs. A bar is the median over draws of the clade's median index value; p is the median over draws of a one-sided Wilcoxon test that Mucorales pairs are more scrambled than Mortierellales pairs.")}
fig("fig_mesosynteny_main.png")
```

Mortierellales and Umbelopsidales keep long collinear diagonals between
closely related genomes (Figure 1A, top). In Mucorales, pairs of similar or
smaller divergence already show the mesosyntenic pattern: genes stay on the
homologous chromosome, but order is broken into short, often inverted
segments. At d ≈ 0.45, Mortierellales and Umbelopsidales still show
recognisable diagonals made of rearranged blocks. *M. plumbeus* vs
*M. lanceolatus* shows only clouds of dots within chromosome-pair boxes.

More closely related pairs are in Supplementary Figure S1: within-species
*Mucor* strain pairs at d = 0.02-0.06 are already strongly rearranged.

## Decay rates and tests

```{r table-tests}
tests %>%
  filter(genome_set == "all", divergence == "d_sub", model == "stretched") %>%
  select(index, comparison, median_p, frac_draws_p05) %>%
  left_join(mtests %>% select(index, comparison, matched_p = median_p), by = c("index", "comparison")) %>%
  mutate(Scale = scale_of[index], Index = idx_lab[index],
         `p (rates)` = fmt_p(median_p), `draws p<0.05` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * frac_draws_p05),
         `p (matched d<=0.15)` = fmt_p(matched_p)) %>%
  arrange(factor(index, levels = names(idx_lab)), comparison) %>%
  select(Scale, Index, Comparison = comparison, `p (rates)`, `draws p<0.05`, `p (matched d<=0.15)`) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "One-sided tests on phylogenetically independent pairs (median p over draws). 'Rates': per-pair decay rates, CDS distance, all genomes. 'Matched': raw index values of pairs with 0.01 < d <= 0.15. With 3 Umbelopsidales pairs (2 in the matched window), the smallest attainable p for comparisons with Umbelopsidales is about 0.006 (0.025).")
```

```{r table-rates}
rates %>%
  filter(genome_set == "all", divergence == "d_sub", model == "stretched") %>%
  left_join(fits %>% filter(divergence == "d_sub") %>% select(index, clade, beta), by = c("index", "clade")) %>%
  mutate(Index = idx_lab[index], clade = factor(clade, levels = clade_levels),
         rate = sprintf("%.3g (%.3g-%.3g)", median_rate, rate_lo, rate_hi)) %>%
  select(index, Index, clade, rate, beta) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = clade, values_from = rate) %>%
  arrange(factor(index, levels = names(idx_lab))) %>%
  transmute(Index, Mortierellales, Umbelopsidales, Mucorales, `shape beta` = round(beta, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Decay rate lambda per CDS substitution/site: median of per-clade median rates over independent-pair draws (95% range over draws). Higher = faster loss of order.")
```

```{r table-matched}
mvals %>%
  mutate(Index = idx_lab[index], clade = factor(clade, levels = clade_levels),
         v = sprintf("%.2f (n = %d)", median_value, as.integer(pairs_per_draw))) %>%
  select(index, Index, clade, v) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = clade, values_from = v) %>%
  arrange(factor(index, levels = names(idx_lab))) %>%
  select(-index) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Index values among closely related pairs (0.01 < d <= 0.15): median over independent-pair draws (independent pairs per draw).")
```

```{r match-d}
md <- within %>% filter(d_sub > cfg$d_min_rate, d_sub <= 0.15) %>% group_by(clade) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), med_d = median(d_sub))
```

Among all pairs in the matched window, the Mucorales pairs are, if anything, *less*
divergent (median d = `r round(md$med_d[md$clade == "Mucorales"], 3)`) than the
Mortierellales pairs (median d = `r round(md$med_d[md$clade == "Mortierellales"], 3)`),
which makes the comparison conservative.

**Scale of the difference.** Mucorales lose order at the meso scale (strand
orientation, chromosome-wide rank correlation) many times faster than
Mortierellales. Among closely related pairs, local neighbourhoods (GOC,
adjacency) also break faster in Mucorales, but the absolute difference is
small (GOC `r mv("goc_intra_norm", "Mucorales")` vs `r mv("goc_intra_norm", "Mortierellales")`):
most genes keep their immediate neighbours, so Mucorales rearrangements move
and invert blocks of several genes rather than single genes. At d ≈ 0.5,
Mortierellales have lost as many or more local adjacencies than Mucorales
(Supplementary Figure S2), so the micro-scale difference is limited to
recent divergence. Inter-chromosomal exchange (neighbour on the
same chromosome) does not differ between Mucorales and Mortierellales.

**Mortierellales also randomise gene orientation, but more slowly and
without losing global order.** At d ≈ 0.4-0.6 the strand index of
Mortierellales pairs approaches 0, while Kendall's tau stays around 0.5
(Figure 1B, Supplementary Figure S3). This fits many small inversions that
flip genes locally while the chromosome-scale diagonal is kept. Mucorales
lose both.

**Umbelopsidales** keep order at least as well as Mortierellales on every
index. Only 6 genomes and 3 independent pairs are available, so a modest
acceleration cannot be excluded, but the point estimates go in the opposite
direction.

## Sensitivity analyses

```{r table-sens}
sens <- tests %>%
  filter(index %in% c("strand_index_norm", "tau_index_norm", "same_chr")) %>%
  mutate(setting = case_when(
    genome_set == "all" & divergence == "d_sub" & model == "stretched" ~ "1 Primary (all genomes, CDS, stretched)",
    genome_set == "all" & divergence == "d_prot" & model == "stretched" ~ "2 Protein distance",
    genome_set == "all" & divergence == "d_time" & model == "stretched" ~ "3 Time (dated tree)",
    genome_set == "all" & divergence == "d_sub" & model == "exponential" ~ "4 Exponential model (beta = 1)",
    genome_set == "ebpnor" & divergence == "d_sub" & model == "stretched" ~ "5 EBP-Nor genomes only",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(setting)) %>%
  mutate(cell = fmt_p(median_p), Index = idx_lab[index]) %>%
  select(setting, Index, comparison, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = comparison, values_from = cell) %>%
  arrange(setting, Index)
knitr::kable(sens, caption = "Median one-sided p across sensitivity settings. EBP-Nor only: 2 Mortierellales and 1-2 Umbelopsidales independent pairs per draw, so power is low.")
```

Conclusions are unchanged with protein distance, time, or the plain
exponential model. With EBP-Nor genomes only (one annotation pipeline), the
Mucorales vs Mortierellales difference remains for Kendall's tau and the
correlation index but not for the strand index. This set has only two
independent Mortierellales pairs.

```{r fig-forest, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "**Supplementary Figure S4.** Decay rates per clade for all indices and sensitivity settings (median over independent-pair draws, 95% range). Rates of 0 are drawn at 0.001."}
fig("figS_rates_forest.png")
```

# Caveats {#caveats}

1. **One evolutionary contrast.** CENP-C was lost once, on the stem of
   Mucorales. Anything else that changed on that branch could explain the
   faster scrambling just as well: whole-genome duplication in Mucorales,
   Grem-LINE retroelements at centromeres, RNAi/heterochromatin pathways,
   genome and repeat content, life history, frequency of sex. The data show
   a coincidence in timing, not a mechanism. The Umbelopsidales result is
   informative because it separates CENP-A loss from CENP-C loss, but it is
   based on 6 genomes.
2. **Mesosynteny is not specific to centromere change.** Dothideomycetes
   (monocentric, CENP-A present) show the same pattern (Hane et al. 2011).
3. **The strand index has a block-size-dependent floor.** If genes move in
   blocks that keep their internal orientation, the expected index under
   complete scrambling is above the gene-level random expectation used for
   normalisation. Mucorales pairs level off at ~0.05-0.15 rather than 0
   (Figure 1B). This affects deep pairs only. The tests rely on shallow
   pairs, and the tau and correlation indices give the same conclusion.
4. **Rate model.** The stretched-exponential shape was chosen after an
   interim look at the data (D11-D12). With one shape shared by all clades
   it fits poorly in places (Supplementary Figure S5): the Mucorales strand
   index at intermediate divergence and Mortierellales tau/correlation
   among close pairs. Decay is therefore not well described by a single
   rate per clade, and the rate values should be read as summaries, not as
   estimates of a rearrangement rate. The model-free matched-divergence
   test and the plain exponential model give the same conclusions.
5. **Assemblies and annotation.** Public and EBP-Nor genomes differ in
   annotation pipeline. All genomes are highly contiguous (≥ 78% of genes on
   sequences with ≥ 100 genes). Indices are computed per homologous
   sequence pair, so fragmentation reduces anchors rather than adding
   apparent scrambling. Misassemblies would show up as isolated off-diagonal
   blocks, not as the within-box scatter seen in Mucorales.
6. **Pairs selected for maximal independence** favour closely related pairs
   (D13). Rates are normalised by divergence, and the matched-divergence
   test does not rely on the rate model.

# Possible next steps

- Map centromeres (Hi-C contact maps are on NeLS under `data/HiC/mcool`;
  AT-rich, Grem-LINE-associated regions in Mucorales). Then test whether
  rearrangement breakpoints are enriched near centromeres and whether
  centromere positions are conserved within chromosome-pair boxes.
- Count inversions directly (breakpoint graphs, e.g. GenomicBreaks) to
  estimate inversion size distributions per clade. The data here suggest
  small inversions in Mortierellales and larger, more frequent ones in
  Mucorales.
- Add Umbelopsidales genomes, or more closely related Umbelopsidales pairs,
  to raise power for the CENP-A-only contrast.
